answer: The quill test I would run is Hunting licence tenure with wildlife agency attestation: a hunting licence renewed for years and listed in the wildlife agency register, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the lotus compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The basalt grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
